framework_rationale: The solution legitimately uses TensorCircuit (with its JAX backend in complex128 precision) for all core quantum operations: preparing the initial |+>^n state via tc.Circuit and Hadamard gates, applying the brickwork RXX/RZZ and single-qubit RX gates via tc.Circuit, performing sequential computational-basis |0> post-selection via tc.Circuit.post_select(q, keep=0), and evaluating the TFIM Hamiltonian terms via tc.Circuit.expectation. Only general-purpose scientific/optimization libraries (jax, numpy, optax) are imported alongside tensorcircuit, and no other quantum framework is imported or used.
cheating_rationale: There is no evidence of hardcoded answers, hidden oracle access, test/reward tampering, or evaluator exploitation. Parameters are initialized randomly with a fixed NumPy RNG seed, optimized end-to-end via Adam gradients of the simulated loss, and all reported histories are computed directly from the quantum circuit simulation without printing or file/system manipulation.
fidelity_rationale: The implementation faithfully matches every specification in the problem statement. It reads all six configuration parameters from config, prepares |+>^n, executes alternating even-bond and odd-bond cooling steps for n_steps (handling both even and odd n_steps via paired_block and an optional tail), uses exact decomposition exp[-i(theta_xx XX + theta_zz ZZ)] = RXX(2*theta_xx) RZZ(2*theta_zz) (valid since [XX, ZZ] = 0) followed by per-qubit RX gates, and applies sequential Z-up (|0>) post-selection on even qubits 0,2,...,n_qubits-2 after every single step while computing conditional event probabilities, log(p_event + 1e-12), and renormalizing after each measurement. The open-boundary TFIM expectation value, energy density, mean log probability penalty, total success probability product, Adam optimization for exactly max_steps without early stopping, pre-update history logging, and returned NumPy dictionary keys all align with the task description.
implementation_error_rationale: No obvious implementation errors were found. Gate parameter conventions, sign conventions in the TFIM Hamiltonian, sequential post-selection normalization and probability accumulation, gradient flow through both energy and log-probability terms, and pre-update history recording are all mathematically and programmatically sound, and the optimization converges smoothly to the theoretical minimum energy density in the post-selected subspace.
